newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila raises bus fares by 14 to 33 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila raises bus fares by 14 to 33 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' Land Transportation Franchising & Regulatory Board said on Tuesday it had approved a 14 to 33 percent fare increase in buses and mini-buses starting Thursday, November 14.
The fare adjustment came after several transport operators sought for an increase after three successive months of domestic fuel prices increases.
Bus fare in Manila and the main island of Luzon would be raised to 2 pesos each, or by 33 percent from the present 1.50 pesos per passenger for the first four kilometres .
Fare for mini-buses after the minimum fare would be at 4.75 centavos per kilometre (0.6214 miles) from 4.15 centavos per km, or a 14 percent increase.
Fare for buses after the minimum fare would be at 52 centavos per kilometre from 43 centavos per kilometre, up by 21 percent.
Minimum fare for the central and southern islands will be adjusted by 25 percent to 2 pesos for the first four kilometres from 1.60 pesos per passenger.
Mini-bus operators would charge 41.5 centavos per km, up 14 percent from 36.5 centavos.

Bus operators in the central Visayas islands would charge 45 centavos each for the succeeding kilometres, up 22 percent from 37 centavos, while those in Mindanao would charge 45.5 centavos, up 21 percent from the present 37.5 centavos.

"The increase in (mini-buses) and bus fares authorised by the LTFRB is a reasonable balance struck between what is believed to be reasonably affordable to commuters and what is fair and just to the applicants," the board said.
The LTFRB last gave a fare increase last December 14, 1990.
